notable_absence.finding: SECOND KEY FINDING FOR THE STATE-VOCABULARY QUESTION, and it is a near miss rather than a silence. This page uses the phrase 'index state' in prose - 'the Query Service will rely on the current index state' - in a sense that has nothing to do with the promoted index-state enum: it means 'the index's current contents', not a lifecycle value. It then describes rebuild-from-scratch, revert-to-snapshot, rollback, and an index service that 'will not perform any scans until a consistent snapshot is created' - four situations in which an index or an Index Service node is demonstrably in some state - and names not one state value. No 'online', 'building', 'ready', 'pending', 'Active', 'Warmup' or 'Paused'. So both state enums remain unreconciled after this page, and the phrase 'index state' now has a documented third meaning to add to the collision list. Two further absences. (1) No requiresPrivilege or requiresServerRole anywhere, though the page shows CREATE INDEX statements that place replicas on named nodes. (2) The page names no setting, API or UI for the number of index snapshots ('By default, two index snapshots are stored on disk' - by whose default, changeable how, is not said), and none for replica count outside the SQL++ WITH clause: no UI path, no Management API.

cross_component_finding: Six defects and frictions. (1) Grammar: '**Availability**: If one Index Service node is lost, the others continues to provide access' - 'the others continues'. In the page's single most important guarantee. (2) The page's title is 'Index Availability and Performance' but its filename, its anchor and every inbound link call it index-replication; replication is only its first of four sections. index-lifecycle.md links to it as '[Index Consistency](index-replication.md#index-consistency)', i.e. by a third name. (3) Casing splits down the middle of the page: 'Index Service' and 'Data Service' in the first half, 'index service' and 'data service' throughout Index Rollback. Same referents, and it reads as two authors. (4) index-lifecycle.md lists three scan consistency values, this page lists four; whichever is right, one of the two adjacent pages is misleading, and the missing one, statement_plus, is the strongest guarantee on offer. (5) The same two adjacent pages disagree about the name of the setting: 'index consistency' in one bullet on the lifecycle page, 'scan consistency' here, with this page's anchor #index-consistency serving as the target for both. (6) index:index-partitioning versus n1ql:index-partitioning again: this page has a whole section on it under indexes/, and links to a reference page filed under n1ql/. The prefix disagreement in the corpus is a direct reflection of the docs filing one subject in two trees.
cross_product_finding: Two cross-product observations. (1) The page's authority for its own core mechanisms lives outside the Capella tree: DCP failover log and failover both link into server/current, and 'Index Service' links to indexing-overview.md - a Capella hub that, as that page's own extraction records, never names the Index Service in prose at all. So a Capella reader following the Index Service link learns nothing about the Index Service, and following the DCP link leaves Capella entirely. (2) capella:server-group is minted here for a concept the registry lacks in BOTH trees, even though it governs replica placement ('given the number and disposition of Index Service nodes across defined server groups') and is the mechanism behind availability-zone spreading. Sixteen rounds of promotion from server/ pages did not surface it, which suggests server groups are documented somewhere the extraction has not yet reached - probably cluster management rather than indexes. Related: this is the second page in this batch to need a node concept and find only server:node, with no capella:node in the registry, while capella:bucket, capella:scope and capella:collection all exist. The Capella namespace has containers but no hardware.
